transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Eleni (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood CSM); Jordan (CTO, Helion), Maya (Head of AI), Priya (Infra), Luis (Product)

Summary: quick QBR and health check, focus on rising token cost on customer support routing, discuss Dedicated/reserved capacity as option, review incident and ask for security docs.

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is the QBR / health check we had scheduled, I see Jordan, Maya, Priya and Luis on the call, thanks for making time
00:08 Jordan: yeah thanks Samir, got a lot going on - hoping to understand costs better and talk through Dedicated options
00:15 Eleni: hi all - quick intro from me, I'm the SE supporting Helion, I can run the throughput and latency bench and look at the KV cache patterns, etc
00:25 Maya: thanks, and real quick, our usage up roughly 30% q over q, mostly from the new returns flow and the conversational customer support route
00:34 Noah: noted, we've flagged those routes in the QBR deck, you'll see per-route token breakdown that shows the support bot is the cost driver
00:44 Priya: curious, can you walk through the recent outage in May? we saw a spike in 99th pct latency and some errors
00:52 Eleni: sure - quick recap, on May 12th we had a region-level networking flakiness that caused retries to pile up, a few requests hit the fallback model which increased cost and latency. Our postmortem shows it was an infra provider blip and Redwood routing fell back to multi-region which added ~400ms on median for effected requests
01:14 Jordan: ok that matches our logs, the main ask is: if we move to Dedicated, can you guarantee no noisy neighbor and better SLOs?
01:23 Samir: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and isolation, yes the whole point is predictable throughput and isolation. We also offer burst capacity config for occasional peaks. SLA is different for Dedicated - we can share the SLA terms
01:36 Luis: and pricing? we need per-token and reserved capacity numbers - our finance wants to model 12-month commit
01:44 Samir: I'll send the reserved capacity pricing matrix after this call, including an example calc based on current qps and token/sec distribution
01:51 Maya: also, for Dedicated how much work is on our side for VPC and KMS integration? we have strict key management requirements
01:58 Eleni: for Dedicated in VPC mode we support customer KMS/HSM integration, there is a bit of networking and IAM work - typical steps: VPC peering or private link, SAML/SSO config, and KMS key provisioning. We can share network diagrams and our KMS integration guide (there's a versioning note for rotating keys)
02:20 Priya: perfect, send the diagrams. also latency - can you run a benchmark with our sample traffic? our median needs to be under 80ms for the support route
02:30 Eleni: yes, we can run bench with your traffic profile. couple notes: quantization and batching configs matter a lot for token cost vs latency; for low-latency route we recommend smaller batch sizes and prefix caching which maintains latency while saving cost for repeated queries
02:51 Jordan: prefix caching? we thought KV cache was internal - how does that get shared across requests for us?
02:58 Eleni: KV cache lives in the serving layer; we expose cache-friendly model variants and you can enable prefix caching at route-level for user context. It's automatic in many cases but we can tune TTLs. Note transcriptions / docs sometimes call it KV chache or K V cache, I see that in older notes
03:18 Maya: ha yeah we've seen the typo in the docs. Ok, on security side we need SOC2 cert, audit logs, and SAML SSO, can you confirm current coverage?
03:26 Samir: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, we provide structured audit logs and SSO via SAML, plus RBAC. For Private deployments we can support additional compliance controls and on-prem. I'll attach the security pack
03:38 Priya: do you do field-level encryption or just at-rest plus KMS?
03:43 Samir: at-rest with customer-managed KMS is supported; field-level encryption is on roadmap and we can talk about tokenization patterns in the deep-dive
03:52 Luis: roadmap items - any features in next quarter that help reduce token usage or better observability?
03:58 Eleni: yes: we're rolling out per-token route sampling, improved token-level cost breakdown in Console, and an Optimize suggestion engine that recommends quantization profiles and batching settings per route. Should help ring-fence expensive flows
04:22 Jordan: good. For the reliability incident, is there a recommended fallback policy? we want graceful degradation not full errors
04:30 Eleni: common approach: route-level fallback to a smaller or cached model, plus region failover with warm standbys, and degrade to summary-only responses for long contexts. We can propose a policy for your support route that prioritizes latency over full-generation quality for time-sensitive flows
04:51 Maya: that sounds reasonable. Next up, procurement timeline - if we want Dedicated, we need a POC and benchmark before procurement approves a multi-month commit. Can Redwood run a 2-week POC?
04:59 Samir: yes, we typically do a 1-2 week Proof-of-Performance, run with sample traffic, measure latency and cost, optionally run some A/B vs hosted. Eleni will coordinate the test harness
05:14 Eleni: for the POC we'll need a traffic dump and a small test dataset, ideally a 24-48 hour sample to reproduce real batching and KV cache hit rates. Also we'll need a contact with infra access for VPC peering during the test if we do Dedicated in VPC mode
05:32 Maya: I'll assemble that and share by 2026-07-19
05:36 Samir: great. On pricing, I'll send an example 12-month reserved capacity worksheet, and include a sensitivity analysis for 10/20/30% growth scenarios
05:47 Jordan: perfect. A few quick product asks: better developer SDK docs for streaming and function calling - our engineers hit some edge cases
05:56 Eleni: noted, we'll loop in DevEx to update the streaming examples. Also we'll share the function-calling best-practices guide
06:05 Luis: last Q on analytics - can we get per-route SLO dashboards in Console?
06:10 Noah: yes, Console supports per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown, we can turn on a 90-day retention for your account as an add-on if you want the history
06:22 Priya: cost concern - if we stay hosted and usage keeps growing, cost projections look scary. Are there quick levers we can apply now to reduce token spend?
06:31 Eleni: yes: 1) enable prefix and KV caching on the support route, 2) tune decoding params (top-p/temperature) to reduce token length, 3) enable quantized model variants for less-critical routes, 4) implement few-shot prompt templating to reduce context tokens. We can provide an Optimize configuration with expected savings estimates
06:56 Maya: can you quantify savings for caching vs quantization? ballpark?
07:01 Eleni: ballpark: caching can save 20-50% on repeated queries, quantization gives 30-40% cost reduction for throughput-heavy, but may add small latency or affect quality; we'll include per-route sim numbers in the Optimize suggestions
07:24 Jordan: ok, this is helpful. Let's recap next steps
07:29 Samir: recap: Samir sends pricing and reserved capacity worksheet, Eleni runs benchmark with Maya's dataset, Noah shares QBR slides and Console usage export, Maya provides traffic sample and infra contact; we'll aim to have POC plan and pricing by 7/22
07:46 Maya: sounds good
07:48 Priya: thanks all
07:50 Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and schedule the benchmark session
07:55 Meeting end

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (KV chache, etc.) consistent with Fireflies exports. References to docs: security pack (will be shared), QBR deck (Noah), reserved capacity pricing worksheet (Samir), benchmark harness (Eleni).
